title: Application of machine learning in the discovery of antimicrobial peptides: exploring their potential for ulcerative colitis therapy.
summary: Machine-learning-ranked peptide candidates had measured antimicrobial activity and improved outcomes in a DSS mouse-colitis model; this is preclinical evidence, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Machine-learning sequence prediction/ranking selected candidates for experimental testing; this is the operation linked to the measured outcomes.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: Selected peptides showed measured antimicrobial activity/stability; treatment improved symptoms and tissue measures in DSS mouse colitis and altered microbiome/metabolites.
evidence.unknown: In-vitro assays and a mouse colitis model test candidates; evidence is short-term and preclinical, not human efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning sequence prediction/ranking selected candidates for experimental testing; this is the operation linked to the measured outcomes.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
